newsitem.title: UK: BP shares helped by bullish chart breakout.
newsitem.headline: BP shares helped by bullish chart breakout.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum continued to be helped on Wednesday by a recent chart breakout above the 700p level, technical analysts said.
The shares were up 8-1/2p at 732-1/2p by 1027 GMT in trade of 2.3 million shares.

Chart watchers said sentiment towards the shares had improved since BP's share price chart had created a bullish ascending triangle pattern and the stock broke above 700p for the first time on January 10.
Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities said the price target from this chart pattern is around 770p.

Analysts at Salomon Brothers said they had picked the stock as one of the most likely to outperform during 1997. Market sources said ABN Amro Hoare Govett was also positive on BP but the analyst was unavailable for immediate comment.
BP shares had been trapped below 700p since October last year, falling as low as 634p.

Glydon noted that BP was also close to a breakout on the relative performance chart, which compares BP's progress with that of the FTSE 100 index. "The stock is in a solid uptrend and we are waiting to see if it makes a new relative high," Glydon said. "If it does, we will probably raise our target."
